The '''2020–21 [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]] season''' was the club's [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|117th season]] in existence and the [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time table|90th consecutive season]] in the top flight of [[Football in Spain|Spanish football]]. In addition to the [[2020–21 La Liga|domestic league]], Real Madrid participated in this season's editions of the [[2020–21 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]], the [[2020–21 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]], and the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]. The season covered the period from 8 August 2020 to 30 June 2021.

Real Madrid played the entire season at the [[Alfredo Di Stéfano Stadium]], while the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]] was undergoing a structural renovation.

Despite finishing a close second in the league and advancing to the Champions League semi-finals for the first time since [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|2018]], Real Madrid went trophyless for the first time since the [[2009–10 Real Madrid CF season|2009–10 season]].

This was the first season since [[2013–14 Real Madrid CF season|2013–14]] without the Colombian midfielder [[James Rodriguez]], who departed for [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], and the first since the [[2012-13 Real Madrid CF season|2012–13]] not to feature [[Gareth Bale]], who was loaned to his previous club [[Tottenham Hotspur]], thus returning to Los Merengues  in the following campaign.

==Summary==
===September===
The first [[2020–21 La Liga|league]] match of the season, on 20 September, ended in a goalless draw at [[Real Sociedad]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/r-sociedad-vs-r-madrid/cronica/2020/09/20/5f67c26246163f4f2e8b4593.html|title=Real Madrid start with stalemate in San Sebastian|publisher=marca.com|date=20 September 2020|access-date=20 September 2020}}</ref> On 26 September, Real secured their first win of the season by defeating [[Real Betis]] 3–2 away from home, with goals from [[Federico Valverde]], [[Sergio Ramos]] and an own goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/54308072|title=Real Betis 2–3 Real Madrid|publisher=bbc.com|date=26 September 2020|access-date=26 September 2020}}</ref> Four days later, a [[Vinícius Júnior]] goal clinched the three points against [[Real Valladolid]] in the first home game of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2020/09/30/football/1601488937_533569.html|title=Real Madrid 1–0 Real Valladolid: Vinicius off the bench to score|publisher=en.as.com|date=30 September 2020|access-date=30 September 2020|archive-date=21 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021074547/https://en.as.com/en/2020/09/30/football/1601488937_533569.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===October===
On 4 October, goals from Vinícius and [[Karim Benzema]] got Madrid another three points in a 2–0 away victory against [[Levante UD|Levante]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/54343523|title=Levante 0–2 Real Madrid|publisher=bbc.com|date=4 October 2020|access-date=4 October 2020}}</ref> After the international break, Madrid lost a home game to [[Cádiz CF|Cádiz]] 0–1 on 17 October.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.co.uk/football/liga/2020-2021/real-madrid-v-cadiz-follow-live_sto7953426/story.shtml|title=Real Madrid suffer shock home defeat to Cadiz|publisher=eurosport.com|date=17 October 2020|access-date=17 October 2020}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid fell 2–3 to [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhrtar Donetsk]] in their opening [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] match, despite second half goals from Modrić and Vinícius after being down 0–3.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2020/10/21/football/1603294516_484511.html|title=Shakhtar Donetsk cling on for shock away win over Real Madrid|publisher=en.as.com|date=21 October 2020|access-date=24 October 2020|archive-date=24 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201024030028/https://en.as.com/en/2020/10/21/football/1603294516_484511.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> The first [[El Clásico]] of the season was played on 24 October, with Madrid winning 3–1 at [[Camp Nou]]. Valverde, Ramos and Modrić scored the goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=582139|title=Real Madrid overcome Barcelona 3–1 in entertaining El Clasico|work=espn.com|date=24 October 2020|access-date=24 October 2020}}</ref> Three days later, Benzema and [[Casemiro]] scored two late goals to give Real a 2–2 draw in the Champions League at [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2020/10/27/football/1603821664_845366.html|title=Borussia Mönchengladbach 2–2 Real Madrid how it happened: Champions League today|publisher=en.as.com|date=27 October 2020|access-date=27 October 2020}}</ref> On the last day of October, a brace from Benzema and goals from Valverde and [[Eden Hazard]] secured a 4–1 home win over [[SD Huesca|Huesca]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Hazard scores as Real win to go top|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54761832|access-date=31 October 2020}}</ref>

===November===
The new month kicked off with a 3–2 home win against [[Inter Milan]] in the Champions League on 3 November. The goalscorers were Benzema, Ramos and [[Rodrygo]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en-in/news/sergio-ramos-100-real-madrid-goals/1jara3o41f8p81uvwv8bsfn4qq |title=Sergio Ramos nets 100th Real Madrid goal with Inter strike in Champions League |website=Goal.com |date=3 November 2020 }}</ref> Five days later, despite an opening goal from Benzema, Madrid lost 1–4 to [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] away from home, while giving up three penalties and an own goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.besoccer.com/new/history-made-as-madrid-concede-3-penalties-and-go-4-1-down-912594|title=History made as Madrid concede 3 penalties and go 4–1 down!|website=besoccer.com|date=8 November 2020}}</ref> On 21 November, after the second international break, Real came away with a 1–1 draw at [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]], despite getting an early lead after a goal from [[Mariano Díaz|Mariano]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55030951|title=Real Madrid held to draw by Villarreal|website=bbc.com|date=21 November 2020}}</ref> Four days later, an early penalty from Hazard and an own goal secured three points in the away Champions League match against Inter.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11945/12142335/inter-milan-0-2-real-madrid-eden-hazard-scores-first-champions-league-goal-for-los-blancos-as-arturo-vidal-sees-red |title=Inter Milan 0–2 Real Madrid: Eden Hazard scores first Champions League goal for Los Blancos as Arturo Vidal sees red |website=Sky Sports |date=25 November 2020 }}</ref> The home match against [[Deportivo Alavés]] was lost 1–2 on 28 November, with Casemiro scoring the lone goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2020/11/28/football/1606587089_914326.html|title=Real Madrid 1–2 Alaves result, summary and goals: LaLiga 2020–21|website=en.as.com|date=28 November 2020|access-date=29 November 2020|archive-date=9 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201209012932/https://en.as.com/en/2020/11/28/football/1606587089_914326.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===December===
On the first day of the new month, Madrid once again lost to Donetsk in the Champions League, this time 0–2 on the road.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55134407|title=Shakhtar Donetsk 2–0 Real Madrid|website=bbc.com|date=1 December 2020}}</ref> Four days later, [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] was defeated 1–0 at the [[Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium|Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán]], thanks to an own goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/sevilla-vs-r-madrid/cronica/2020/12/05/5fcbc18be2704ecfbb8b457c.html|title=Real Madrid step up in Seville|website=marca.com|date=5 December 2020}}</ref> On 9 December, Madrid defeated Borussia Mönchengladbach in the Champions League 2–0 at home, with Benzema scoring both goals. With the win, Madrid topped Group B and advanced to the knockout stage.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0264-110d24852716-8f57c96e16c8-1000--knockout-line-up-complete|title=Real Madrid lead seven through to complete last-16 line-up|website=[[UEFA]]|date=9 December 2020}}</ref> Three days later, a Casemiro goal and an own goal gave Real a 2–0 home victory over [[Atlético Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55217123|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Atlético Madrid|website=bbc.com|date=12 December 2020}}</ref> On 15 December, a brace from Benzema and a goal from [[Toni Kroos]] saw Madrid get away with another home win, this time defeating [[Athletic Bilbao]] 3–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/real-madrid-vs-athletic-bilbao-score-karim-benzema-shines-for-los-blancos-in-la-liga-win/|title=Real Madrid vs. Athletic Bilbao score: Karim Benzema shines for Los Blancos in La Liga win|website=cbssports.com|date=15 December 2020}}</ref> Goals from Benzema, Modrić and Vázquez helped Madrid to a 3–1 away win over [[SD Eibar|Eibar]], moving the team to second place.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/eibar-vs-r-madrid/cronica/2020/12/20/5fdfcb0b268e3e85238b45be.html|title=Benzema leads way for Real Madrid at Eibar|website=marca.com|date=20 December 2020}}</ref> On 23 December, Real Madrid secured a 2–0 home win against [[Granada CF|Granada]], with Casemiro and Benzema on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://depor.com/futbol-internacional/espana/directv-real-madrid-vs-granada-en-vivo-directo-online-gratis-por-directv-sports-sky-sports-y-movistar-minuto-a-minuto-e-incidencias-por-laliga-santander-nczd-noticia|title=Continúa al acecho del Atlético: Real Madrid derrotó 2–0 al Granada por LaLiga Santander|website=depor.com|date=23 December 2020}}</ref> A week later, in the last game of 2020, a Modrić goal was not enough as Madrid drew [[Elche CF|Elche]] 1–1 away from home to finish the year in second place.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://onefootball.com/de/news/elche-1-1-real-madrid-another-modric-golazo-and-a-draw-at-elche-to-end-2020-32071562|title=Elche 1–1 Real Madrid – Another Modrić golazo and a draw at Elche to end 2020|website=onefootball.com|date=30 December 2020}}</ref>

===January===
Real started the new year with a 2–0 win over [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]] at the Alfredo Di Stéfano on 2 January. The goals were scored by Vázquez and [[Marco Asensio]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-spain-mad-clv-report/real-madrid-see-off-celta-to-return-to-la-liga-summit-idUKKBN2970N4|title=Real Madrid see off Celta to return to La Liga summit|website=reuters.com|date=2 January 2021}}</ref> A week later, the match at [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] ended in a goalless draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2020-2021/osasuna-v-real-madrid-la-liga-live_sto8057423/story.shtml|title=Real Madrid miss chance to go top in goalless draw at Osasuna|website=eurosport.com|date=9 January 2021}}</ref> On 14 January, Madrid lost the semi-final of the [[2020–21 Supercopa de España]] against Athletic Bilbao 1–2, with a second half goal from Benzema not being enough.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12188145/real-madrid-1-2-athletic-bilbao-spanish-super-cup-holders-knocked-out-after-raul-garcia-double|title=Real Madrid 1–2 Athletic Bilbao: Spanish Super Cup holders knocked out after Raul Garcia double|website=skysports.com|date=14 January 2021}}</ref> Real was knocked out of the [[2020–21 Copa del Rey]] in the round of 32 exactly six days later, after losing 1–2 {{aet}} at [[CD Alcoyano|Alcoyano]], where [[Éder Militão]] initially gave Madrid the lead.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55722360|title=Alcoyano 2–1 Real Madrid: Third division side cause huge upset|website=bbc.com|date=21 January 2021}}</ref> On 23 January, Real defeated Alavés 4–1 on the road, with a brace from Benzema and goals from Casemiro and Hazard.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.trtworld.com/sport/real-madrid-smash-alaves-4-1-away-at-mendizorroza-43522|title=Real Madrid smash Alaves 4–1 away at Mendizorroza|website=trtworld.com|date=23 January 2021}}</ref> A week later, ten-man Madrid lost the home match against Levante 1–2, even though Asensio gave Real an early lead.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12203769/real-madrids-la-liga-title-hopes-suffer-huge-blow-with-shock-levante-loss-euro-round-up|title=Real Madrid's La Liga title hopes suffer huge blow with shock Levante loss - Euro round-up|website=skysports.com|date=30 January 2021}}</ref>

===February===
A brace from [[Raphaël Varane]] helped produce a 2–1 come-from-behind win at Huesca on 6 February.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/varane-bags-brace-as-real-madrid-come-from-behind-to-beat-huesca-32330182|title=Varane bags brace as Real Madrid come from behind to beat Huesca|website=onefootball.com|date=6 February 2021}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid hosted [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] and won 2–0 after goals from Benzema and [[Ferland Mendy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2020-2021/liga-updates-real-madrid-v-getafe-cf-live_sto8112056/story.shtml|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Getafe: Zinedine Zidane's side win to cut Atletico Madrid's lead to five points|website=eurosport.com|date=9 February 2021}}</ref> On 14 February, goals from Benzema and Kroos secured another three points in a 2–0 home win against Valencia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56064499|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Valencia|website=bbc.com|date=14 February 2021}}</ref> Six days later, a second-half Casemiro goal helped Madrid to a 1–0 win over Valladolid at the [[Estadio José Zorrilla|José Zorrilla]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football24.news/soccer/62800/real-madrid-defeats-valladolid-0-1-with-a-goal-from-casemiro-in-the-spanish-league-international-football-sports.html|title=Real Madrid defeats Valladolid 0–1 with a goal from Casemiro in the Spanish League|website=football24.com|date=20 February 2021|access-date=21 February 2021|archive-date=7 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210407014446/https://www.football24.news/soccer/62800/real-madrid-defeats-valladolid-0-1-with-a-goal-from-casemiro-in-the-spanish-league-international-football-sports.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 24 February, [[Atalanta B.C.|Atalanta]] was defeated 1–0 in [[Bergamo]], thanks to a goal from Mendy, in the first leg of the Champions League round of 16.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2021/feb/24/atalanta-v-real-madrid-champions-league-last-16-live |title=Atalanta v Real Madrid: Champions League last 16 – as it happened |website=The Guardian |date=24 February 2021 }}</ref>

===March===
On the first day of the new month, the home game against Sociedad ended in a 1–1 draw, with the goal coming from Vinícius in the closing minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/vinicius-junior-scores-in-real-sociedad-draw-as-he-earns-100th-real-madrid-cap-1614645335000|title=Vinicius Junior scores in Real Sociedad draw as he earns 100th Real Madrid cap|website=fourfourtwo.com|date=1 March 2021}}</ref> In a derby against Atlético at the [[Metropolitano Stadium|Wanda Metropolitano]] on 7 March, Benzema scored a late equalizer with the same result, securing Madrid a point.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.news18.com/news/sports/la-liga-madrid-derby-ends-in-draw-real-score-late-to-hold-atletico-3509066.html|title=La Liga: Madrid Derby Ends in Draw, Real Score Late to Hold Atletico|website=news18.com|date=7 March 2021}}</ref> Six days later, a brace from Benzema gave Madrid a 2–1 come-from-behind victory over Elche at the Di Stéfano.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2021/03/13/benzema-brace-leads-madrid-fightback-in-2-1-win-over-elche/115555782/|title=Benzema brace gives Madrid 2-1 win, Atlético held at Getafe|website=usatoday.com|date=13 March 2021}}</ref> On 16 March, Madrid secured their qualification for the quarter-finals of the Champions League with a 3–1 home win over Atalanta. The goals were scored by Benzema, Ramos and Asensio.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2021/03/16/football/1615919558_181148.html|title=Real Madrid 3–1 Atalanta (4–1): goals, result, summary Champions League 2020/21|website=as.com|date=16 March 2021|access-date=19 March 2021|archive-date=19 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210319005326/https://en.as.com/en/2021/03/16/football/1615919558_181148.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Four days later, a brace from Benzema and a goal from Asensio saw Madrid win 3–1 at Celta Vigo.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2020-2021/football-news-celta-vigo-v-real-madrid-follow-live_sto8183411/story.shtml|title=Celta Vigo 1–3 Real Madrid: Karim Benzema brace sees Real Madrid leapfrog Barcelona in Liga|website=eurosport.com|date=20 March 2021}}</ref>

===April===
On 3 April, Real defeated Eibar 2–0 at home with goals from Asensio and Benzema.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210403-real-madrid-see-off-eibar-ahead-of-liverpool-and-barca-tests|title=Real Madrid see off Eibar ahead of Liverpool and Barca tests|website=france24.com|date=3 April 2021}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid defeated [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] 3–1 at the Di Stéfano in the crucial first leg of the Champions League quarter-finals. Vinícius scored a brace, with another goal coming from Asensio.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0268-11fa6c6b579a-34f1dc121385-1000--real-madrid-3-1-liverpool-vinicius-junior-strikes-twice/ |title=Real Madrid 3–1 Liverpool: Vinícius Júnior strikes twice |website=UEFA |date=6 April 2021 }}</ref> The season's second El Clásico was won 2–1 on 10 April with goals from Benzema and Kroos.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/56449503|title=La Liga: Real Madrid beat Barca to move top of table|website=bbc.com|date=10 April 2021}}</ref> Four days later, the return leg against Liverpool ended 0–0, meaning Madrid qualified for the Champions League semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0268-120a8423aa8b-b034028ae485-1000--liverpool-0-0-real-madrid-merengues-hold-firm-to-eliminate/ |title=Liverpool 0–0 Real Madrid: Merengues hold firm to eliminate Reds |website=UEFA |date=14 April 2021 }}</ref> On 18 April, Real were held to a goalless draw at Getafe.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2020-2021/getafe-v-real-madrid-la-liga-live_sto8275060/story.shtml|title=Real Madrid lose momentum in title race with Getafe draw|website=eurosport.com|date=18 April 2021}}</ref> Three days later, a brace from Benzema and a goal from [[Álvaro Odriozola]] gave Madrid a 3–0 away victory over Cádiz.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2020-2021/cadiz-v-real-madrid-live-la-liga-updates_sto8280422/story.shtml|title=Karim Benzema hits brace as Real Madrid ease past Cadiz and go top of La Liga|website=eurosport.com|date=21 April 2021}}</ref> The crucial home match against Betis on 24 April 2021 ended in a 0–0 draw, damaging Real's title aspirations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56873233|title=Real Madrid 0–0 Real Betis|website=bbc.com|date=24 April 2021}}</ref> Three days later, a Benzema goal secured a 1–1 home draw against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in the first leg of the Champions League semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/apr/27/real-madrid-chelsea-champions-league-semi-final-match-report|title=Pulisic gives Chelsea the edge with draw at Real Madrid in semi-final first leg|website=theguardian.com|date=27 April 2021}}</ref>

===May===
On 1 May, Militao and Casemiro scored late to help Madrid post a 2–0 home win versus Osasuna.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.in/football/report/_/gameId/581870|title=Real Madrid win to keep pace in La Liga race|website=espn.in|date=1 May 2021}}</ref> Four days later, Real's Champions League campaign came to an end at the semi-final stage after a 0–2 away loss to Chelsea.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4214711/2021/05/05/chelsea-beat-real-madrid-to-set-up-champions-league-final-against-man-city/|title=Chelsea beat Real Madrid to set up Champions League final against Man City|website=theathletic.com|date=5 May 2021}}</ref> Another four days later, an Asensio goal and a late deflection from Hazard helped Madrid salvage a point in the home game against Sevilla, keeping them alive in the title race.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210509-real-madrid-strike-late-but-title-hopes-hit-by-dramatic-sevilla-draw|title=Real Madrid strike late but title hopes hit by dramatic Sevilla draw|website=france24.com|date=9 May 2021}}</ref> The away match against Granada on 13 May was won 4–1, with goals coming from Modrić, Rodrygo, Odriozola and Benzema.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-espana.net/2021/05/13/real-madrid-beat-granada-4-1-to-keep-la-liga-title-ambition-alive|title=Real Madrid beat Granada 4–1 to keep La Liga title ambition alive|website=football-espana.net|date=13 May 2021}}</ref> Three days later, a goal from Nacho secured Madrid a 1–0 win at Athletic Bilbao. With that win, Real stayed in second position, two points behind leaders Atlético Madrid, with one match to go.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2021/05/16/football/1621176948_141264.html|title=Athletic Bilbao 0–1 Real Madrid result, goals, summary|website=en.as.com|date=16 May 2021}}</ref> On 22 May, Madrid produced a late comeback to defeat Villarreal 2–1 at home in the last match of the season, with Benzema and Modrić scoring the goals. Since Atlético also won their game, Real finished second in the standings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://uk.sports.yahoo.com/news/soccer-real-madrid-beat-villarreal-180538194.html|title=Soccer-Real Madrid beat Villarreal but end season second|website=uk.sports.yahoo.com|date=22 May 2021}}</ref> This marked the club's first trophyless season since [[2009–10 Real Madrid CF season|2009–10]].<ref name="trophyless">{{cite web |date=22 May 2021 |title=Atletico Madrid crowned champions as Real Madrid go trophyless for first time since 2010 |url=https://www.goal.com/en-ph/news/atletico-madrid-crowned-champions-as-real-madrid-go/t28ap0z5hif71oedx311o5yfc |access-date=22 May 2021 |website=Goal}}</ref>
